outcome_intro: Running Sophos Central for a book of customers? Ask your AI "what needs attention across every customer today," "which machines have tamper protection off," or "isolate WS-FIN-07" and get one answer instead of opening each tenant from the Partner Dashboard. One command refreshes every customer tenant into a local store, so triage, health ranking, gap checks and billing reconciliation run across the whole book at once.

pain_points: Sophos Central is tenant-by-tenant underneath. A partner credential has to list its tenants, then call each tenant's own regional API host with an X-Tenant-ID header (Sophos's own partner getting-started guide walks through that loop). The Partner Dashboard rolls up alerts, but the questions behind them - which machines are unhealthy, whose tamper protection is off, whose health score slipped - still mean drilling into one customer at a time.

Home-grown scripts stop at one tenant. Community tooling is usually written for a single customer: the SophosCentral-Powershell module says outright "There is currently no support for multiple tenants", and multi-tenant support sits on its to-do list. Every MSP ends up rewriting the same tenant loop, region routing and paging.

Monthly billing and coverage reconciliation is manual. Matching the partner usage report to what is actually deployed per customer, spotting licences used beyond their quantity or about to expire, and finding devices that are unlicensed or unencrypted means exporting and stitching data by hand.

different_vs_wrappers: Live MCP wrappers for Sophos Central, such as [rijul170/sophos-central-mcp](https://github.com/rijul170/sophos-central-mcp), take a tenant ID on each call and answer one tenant at a time. This connector also resolves the caller with whoami and routes every tenant call to that tenant's regional host for you, but its fleet commands first refresh every customer tenant into a local SQLite store with a per-tenant ok/forbidden/error ledger, so a book-wide question (triage, health ranking, gaps) is one local query the agent reads as a finished answer, billing is joined to the deployed endpoints already in that store, and the next refresh shows what changed.
different_vs_vendor: It complements the Sophos Central Partner Dashboard rather than replacing it: the dashboard stays the place for policy authoring, investigations and Sophos's own consolidated alert view, while this skill brings cross-customer triage, health ranking, gap checks, tamper remediation and billing reconciliation to whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, and sophos-central-mcp speaks HTTP natively: run `sophos-central-mcp --transport http` with SOPHOS_CENTRAL_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN set (it serves `http://127.0.0.1:7777/mcp` and requires that token as a bearer header) and put that endpoint behind an HTTPS tunnel or your own reverse proxy. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.

faqs.q: Is my Sophos Central data safe?
faqs.a: Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, MCP server, and the local mirror are all local. The AI sees query results, not raw bulk data, and credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.q: What Sophos Central API credential do I need?
faqs.a: An API credential (a service principal) created in Sophos Central: in the Partner Dashboard under Settings & Policies > API Credentials for a partner, or under Global Settings > API Credentials Management for an organization or a single customer. Set SOPHOS_CENTRAL_CLIENT_ID and SOPHOS_CENTRAL_CLIENT_SECRET. The role you give it is the real permission boundary: Service Principal Read-Only covers every report here but cannot run Live Discover queries; writes such as isolation, scans and tamper protection need a role that allows them.

faqs.q: Does it work with a partner, organization and single-tenant credential?
faqs.a: Yes. whoami tells the CLI which kind of credential it holds. A partner or organization credential walks every customer tenant in the fleet commands, and picks one customer with --tenant (or SOPHOS_CENTRAL_TENANT_ID) for tenant-scoped commands such as endpoints or alerts. A single-tenant credential works on its own tenant.

faqs.q: Will this hit Sophos Central API rate limits?
faqs.a: Calls go through a shared throttle of 1.5 requests per second by default (--rate-limit), under Sophos's own limits. fleet refresh --plan prints the tenant count and estimated calls and time before you run it. After a refresh, fleet triage, fleet health and fleet gaps read the local store and make no API calls.

faqs.q: Why do some customers show as forbidden?
faqs.a: Sophos returns 403 to a partner for trial tenants and for term customers without Partner Assistance. fleet refresh records those in its per-tenant ledger and carries on, and fleet triage lists them as blind tenants so you can see what was not read. Trial tenants are skipped unless you pass --include-trial. A full refresh (no --tenant) also removes what earlier fleet refreshes stored for tenants it no longer covers (offboarded tenants, and trial tenants when --include-trial is not set), so fleet reports always match your last full refresh.

faqs.q: Can the AI isolate a machine or turn tamper protection back on by itself?
faqs.a: Only if you let it. contain and fleet tamper print a plan and change nothing without --yes, and the MCP server never passes --yes, so those two only preview over MCP. But the MCP server's generic sophos-central_execute tool can call any Sophos Central endpoint except the six that return a password or token, including isolation, scans and policy changes, gated only by your AI app's approval prompt. If an agent should only read, set SOPHOS_CENTRAL_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 in the MCP server's environment: it refuses every non-GET call and hides the sync and export tools. Keep the approval prompt on, and give the API credential a read-only role.

faqs.q: Does it cover Sophos XDR or MDR Cases and Detections?
faqs.a: Not in this version. It covers the REST APIs: alerts, endpoints, policies, exclusions, Live Discover, XDR Data Lake queries, SIEM events and alerts, Account Health Check, licences and partner billing. Cases and Detections are not included.

faqs.q: Does it replace the Sophos Central Partner Dashboard?
faqs.a: No. The dashboard stays best for policy authoring, investigations and day-to-day console work. This skill answers the across-every-customer questions and runs scripted actions from your AI agent.

governance_summary: The skill authenticates with a Sophos Central API credential you create, and its reach is exactly the role you give that credential. Every fleet report (triage, health, gaps, revenue) and every list or get, except the credential reads named below, is read-only and safe to let an agent run. Sophos Central is also an endpoint security console, so isolating machines, starting scans, collecting forensic logs and memory dumps, running Live Discover queries and changing tamper protection reach real customer machines; those, plus policy, exclusion and allow-list changes that can weaken protection, need a human to approve the exact command. Commands that return a tamper protection password or a migration token are credential reads, kept out of the MCP server and human-only. contain and fleet tamper preview by default and act only with --yes, which the MCP server never passes; the MCP server's generic execute tool can still call any write endpoint except the six that return a password or token, so set SOPHOS_CENTRAL_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 for an agent that should only read.

credentials_note: The client secret stays in your environment (it is written to disk only if you pass auth login --client-secret), and the short-lived access token minted from it is cached in a permission-restricted credentials file on your machine until it expires or you run auth logout
